definition_zh: 明智的；可取的；适当的；建议采用的
definition_en: sensible or proper to do in the circumstances, or recommended by an authority
core_image: 岔路口一块牌子，箭头指向更安全的那条路
scene: 山路开始起雾，向导看了看天色，建议队伍掉头。It is advisable to turn back before the fog gets thicker.
sceneCN: 这里 advisable 是「明智的、可取的」（第 1 个义项：在特定情况下应当做）；句意为在雾变浓之前掉头是明智的。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「建议；通知」
由同一词源构成，义为「建议」
由 advisable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可取性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「明智地」

senses.title: Sensible or wise in the circumstances
senses.definition: sensible and likely to produce a good result in the situation at hand
senses.definitionCN: 在眼前情形中明智、且很可能带来好结果
senses.example: It is advisable to turn back before the fog gets thicker.
senses.exampleCN: 在雾变浓之前掉头是明智的。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns advise into 'worth being advised or recommended', so advisable describes what a sensible adviser would suggest.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把 advise 变成「值得被建议的」，所以 advisable 描述明智的顾问会推荐的做法。

senses.title: Recommended by an authority or professional
senses.titleCN: 建议采用的；合乎专业意见的
senses.definition: recommended as proper by a person or body with expert or official authority
senses.definitionCN: 由具有专业或官方权威的人或机构推荐为妥当
senses.example: Early testing is advisable for anyone with symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何有症状的人来说，尽早检测是可取的做法。
senses.why: What professionals advise becomes advisable, because the word points back to the advice behind it.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士建议的事就成为 advisable，因为这个词回指它背后的建议。

senses.title: Open to advice, in older use
senses.definition: in older English, willing to receive advice; now rare and usually replaced by other words
senses.definitionCN: 在较早英语中，愿意接受劝告；现已罕见，通常用别的词表达
senses.example: The old lord was advisable and changed his plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老领主愿意听劝，改变了自己的计划。
senses.why: The suffix once meant 'able to be advised', before the modern sense of 'worth recommending' took over.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀一度表示「能够被劝告」，后来才被现代义「值得推荐」取代。

intro.en: Advisable is advise plus -able, so its history is the history of advise.
intro.cn: advisable 是 advise 加 -able，所以它的历史就是 advise 的历史。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the deepest root of the family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，是这一词族最深的根。

items.en: Avis meant opinion or view.
items.cn: avis 意为意见或看法。

items.en: The verb advise entered English with the sense of giving an opinion.
items.cn: 动词 advise 以「给出意见」义进入英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded later, built with -able; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词较晚出现，由 -able 构成；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The modern sense settled on 'worth recommending', while the older 'open to advice' sense faded.
items.cn: 现代义固定在「值得推荐」，较老的「愿意听劝」义逐渐消失。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advise family; the near-meaning group gathers words for wise and recommended action.
note.cn: 形近组是 advise 这一族词；近义组收明智与被推荐的说法。

entries.definition: To give advice; the verb with s.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，以 s 结尾，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: An opinion about what to do; the noun with c.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」，以 c 结尾，与本词同源。

entries.definition: The quality of being advisable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可取性」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: A person who gives advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，由 advise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Based on good judgment; practical and wise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的」，强调良好判断。

entries.definition: Careful and wise about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谨慎的」，强调为将来打算。

entries.definition: Suggested as good or proper.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被推荐的」，对应权威建议义项。

entries.definition: Showing experience and good judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的」，最宽泛的对应词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the adjective from advise and its suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 advise 及其后缀出发，拼出这个形容词。

normal.en: Advisable is advise plus -able: worth being advised.
normal.cn: advisable 是 advise 加 -able：值得被建议的。

normal.en: It is advisable to do something means a sensible adviser would tell you to do it.
normal.cn: 「It is advisable to do something」意为明智的顾问会建议你这么做。

normal.en: Highly advisable is a stronger way to say very sensible.
normal.cn: highly advisable 是「非常明智」的更强说法。

normal.en: Not advisable is a polite way to say don't do it.
normal.cn: not advisable 是「别这么做」的委婉说法。

normal.en: The noun advice uses c, the verb advise uses s, and advisable keeps the s of the verb.
normal.cn: 名词 advice 用 c，动词 advise 用 s，而 advisable 保留动词的 s。

abstract.cn: 岔路口一块指向更安全小路的牌子。

abstract.en: A hand gently turning a traveller away from the cliff.

abstract.en: A lamp placed ahead so the next step is visible.
abstract.cn: 一盏放在前方的灯，让下一步看得清。

examples.en: It is advisable to book in advance.
examples.cn: 提前订票是可取的。

examples.en: Exercise is advisable for most patients.

examples.en: Early application is strongly advisable.
examples.cn: 尽早申请是非常可取的。

root: 由动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成。advise 源自拉丁语 visum「所见的」，出自 videre「看」，经古法语 avis「意见」进入英语。核心是「值得被建议的」，因此 advisable 表示「明智的、可取的、建议采用的」；较早还曾有「愿意听劝的」义，现已罕见。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: wise in the situation, recommended by authority, and the older sense of being open to advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：在当下明智、受权威推荐，以及较老的「愿意听劝」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork in the road and a sign pointing toward the safer way.
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口一块指向更安全道路的牌子。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the wise choice depends on the circumstances.
branches.cn: 情境线：明智的选择取决于当下情形。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: professional advice makes an action advisable.
branches.cn: 权威线：专业建议使某项行动成为可取。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: an older word for being willing to take advice.
branches.cn: 旧义线：较早表示「愿意接受劝告」的用法。

branches.en: THE RECOMMENDATION: what is wise and what is advised point the same way.
branches.cn: 推荐线：明智之事与被建议之事指向同一方向。

branches.en: THE POSTURE: taking advice and giving advice meet in one word.
branches.cn: 姿态线：听劝与进言在同一个词中相遇。

intro.en: Advisable is an English verb plus the adjective suffix -able; the verb itself is Latin through Old French.
intro.cn: advisable 是一个英语动词加形容词后缀 -able；动词本身经古法语源自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded; the suffix -able is English and fully productive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，后缀 -able 是英语中能产的后缀。

definition_zh: 顾问；指导者；导师（亦拼作 advisor）
definition_en: a person whose job is to give expert advice, or someone who guides another person's studies or decisions
core_image: 一个人站在你侧后方半步，看着同一份文件替你圈出重点
scene: 学生把选课表摊在桌上，几门课的时间撞在一起，家长也拿不定主意。Her academic adviser helped her rearrange the timetable.
sceneCN: 这里 adviser 指学校里负责指导学生学业的老师（第 2 个义项：学业导师）；句意为她的学业导师帮她重新排了课表。

由本词加名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「顾问职位；顾问身份」

senses.title: A professional consultant
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give expert advice to a company, a government or an individual
senses.definitionCN: 以向公司、政府或个人提供专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The firm hired an adviser to review its energy costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请了一位顾问来审查能源开支。
senses.why: The French verb aviser means to form a view, and the agent suffix -er names the person who does it as a job, so an adviser is the one paid to look and judge.
senses.whyCN: 法语动词 aviser 意为「形成看法」，施事后缀 -er 指以这件事为业的人，所以 adviser 是受雇去看、去判断的那个人。

senses.title: An academic guide
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or university who helps a student choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 学校里帮助学生选课、规划学业的老师
senses.example: Her academic adviser suggested dropping one of the two science courses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的学业导师建议她退掉两门理科课中的一门。
senses.why: In a university the same role narrows to study: the person looks at a student's path and points out the next step.
senses.whyCN: 在大学里，同一个角色缩小到学业上：这个人看着学生的路径，指出下一步该往哪走。

senses.title: Anyone who offers advice
senses.definition: a person, often trusted or senior, who gives another person advice without holding a formal post
senses.definitionCN: 不担任正式职务、却为他人出主意的人，往往是受信任者或长辈
senses.example: Throughout the crisis he remained her closest adviser.
senses.exampleCN: 整个危机期间，他始终是她最亲近的谋士。
senses.why: No job title is needed: whoever is looked to for a view becomes an adviser for that moment.
senses.whyCN: 不需要任何头衔：谁被当成可以拿主意的人，谁在那个时刻就是 adviser。

intro.en: Adviser is the agent noun of the French verb that also gave English advise, and its two spellings reflect two different endings.
intro.cn: adviser 是那个同时带来英语 advise 的法语动词的施事名词，它的两种拼写来自两个不同的词尾。

items.en: Latin videre 'to see' and its participle visum 'what is seen' lie behind the French word; the combination with ad is generally assumed, though the exact derivation is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre「看见」及其分词 visum「所见之物」是法语词的底子；与 ad 的结合一般认为成立，但确切构成并不确定。

items.en: The verb aviser meant to consider and to give an opinion, and from it English took both the verb advise and the idea of the person who advises.
items.cn: 动词 aviser 意为「思量、提出看法」，英语由它既取来动词 advise，也取来「提出看法的人」这一概念。

items.en: English added the native agent suffix -er to the borrowed verb, giving adviser for the person who gives the view.
items.cn: 英语给借来的动词加上本土施事后缀 -er，得到 adviser，指提出看法的人。

items.en: A second spelling, advisor, was formed with the Latin-looking ending -or. Both forms have been in use since the sixteenth century and mean exactly the same thing.
items.cn: 另一种拼写 advisor 用看起来像拉丁语的词尾 -or 构成。两种形式自十六世纪起并用，含义完全相同。

items.en: Adviser is the usual form in British edited prose, while advisor is common in American job titles and organization names; dictionaries treat them as variants, not as different words.
items.cn: 在英国编辑体例中 adviser 更常见，而 advisor 多用于美式职位头衔与机构名称；词典把二者视为异体拼写，而非两个不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the variant spelling and the words built on the same verb; the near-meaning group gathers other people who give guidance, with different degrees of formality.
note.cn: 形近组收异体拼写与同一动词构成的词；近义组收其他提供指导的人，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The same noun spelled with the Latin-looking ending -or, common in job titles and organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，adviser 的另一种拼写，词尾用看起来像拉丁语的 -or，多见于职位头衔与机构名称，读音和含义完全相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give someone advice; the person who does this is the adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「建议、劝告」；执行这个动作的人就是 adviser。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning having the role of giving advice, or a noun for a body that does so.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顾问的、咨询的」；作名词时指提供咨询的机构。

entries.definition: The noun for the opinion itself, ending in c and pronounced with /s/.
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，指意见本身，以 c 结尾、读清音 /s/，与指人的 adviser 分工不同。

entries.definition: An expert who is paid by a company to advise on a particular field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咨询顾问」，指受公司聘请、就某一领域提供意见的专家，职业色彩比 adviser 更强。

entries.definition: A formal word for a legal adviser or for the advice itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「法律顾问」或「忠告」，语气正式，法律色彩明显。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides someone over a long period, usually in work or life rather than in one case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导师、引路人」，指长期指导他人的人，多在工作或人生层面，而非处理单个案子。

entries.definition: A person who shows the way, literally or figuratively; broader and less technical than adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「向导、指导者」，可实指带路的人，也可比喻，范围比 adviser 宽，专业色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French verb, the agent suffix, and the phrases in which this person noun appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的法语动词、施事后缀，以及这个指人的名词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: advise plus -er gives the person who gives the view.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er，就得到给出看法的那个人。

normal.en: Adviser and advisor are one word with two endings: -er is the English agent suffix, -or the Latin-looking one.
normal.cn: adviser 与 advisor 是同一个词的两种词尾：-er 是英语施事后缀，-or 是看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

normal.en: An academic adviser handles courses; a financial adviser handles money.
normal.cn: academic adviser 管选课，financial adviser 管钱。

normal.en: Adviser to the president shows that the role is tied to a person in power.
normal.cn: adviser to the president 说明这个角色依附于掌权者。

normal.en: A consultant is usually hired by a firm, while an adviser may be a trusted friend.
normal.cn: consultant 通常由公司聘用，而 adviser 也可能是身边受信任的朋友。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling the lines that matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看同一页纸，把要紧的几行圈出来。

abstract.en: The adviser does not carry the bag or walk the road; the adviser only makes the map easier to read.
abstract.cn: 顾问不替你背包，也不替你走路；他只是让地图更好读。

abstract.en: The same figure can sit in a palace, a clinic or a dormitory: the setting changes, the half step behind does not.
abstract.cn: 同一个人物可以出现在宫殿、诊所或宿舍：场景变了，那半步的距离不变。

examples.en: The company's legal adviser reviewed the contract.
examples.cn: 公司的法律顾问审阅了这份合同。

examples.en: Academic advisers help students choose their courses.
examples.cn: 学业导师帮助学生选课。

examples.en: She served as an adviser to two mayors.
examples.cn: 她曾担任两任市长的顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德外泽」——阿德站在你侧后方，替你圈出文件上的重点：顾问。

root: 由古法语动词 aviser「思量、提出看法」加英语施事后缀 -er 构成；avis 一般认为出自拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ videre「看」。异体拼写 advisor 借了拉丁语风格的词尾 -or。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses all name the same figure: someone who looks at a situation and points out a way, whether as a paid expert, a study guide, or a trusted voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都指同一种人：看清局势后指出一条路的人，只是身份不同——受聘的专家、学业上的导师，或身边受信任的进言者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person half a step behind you, looking at the same page and circling what matters.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在你侧后方半步，和你看着同一页纸，把要紧处圈出来。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: expert looking is sold as a service to firms and governments.
branches.cn: 职业线：专家的「看」被当作服务，卖给公司与政府。

branches.en: THE CAMPUS: the same looking narrows to courses and study plans.
branches.cn: 校园线：同样的「看」缩小到选课与学习计划上。

branches.en: THE INFORMAL VOICE: no post is needed, only the trust of the person being advised.
branches.cn: 非正式线：不需要职位，只需要被建议者的信任。

branches.en: TRUST IS THE COMMON CORE: paid or unpaid, the adviser is the one whose view is asked for.
branches.cn: 信任是共同内核：无论受聘与否，顾问都是那个被征询看法的人。

branches.en: ONE ROLE, THREE SETTINGS: office, campus and kitchen table all hold the same half step behind.
branches.cn: 一个角色，三处场景：办公室、校园与厨房餐桌旁，都站着同一个「半步之后」的人。

intro.en: Adviser is a borrowed French verb plus an English agent suffix; the second spelling simply swaps in a Latin-looking ending.
intro.cn: adviser 是借来的法语动词加英语施事后缀；另一种拼写只是换了一个看起来像拉丁语的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded, and ad is a recorded preposition; the French verb aviser is also recorded, while the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，ad 也是有记录的介词；法语动词 aviser 同样有记录，更早的印欧词根则属重构形式。

senses.title: A person paid to give expert advice
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give professional advice on money, law, business or policy
senses.definitionCN: 以提供理财、法律、商业或政策方面的专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The company hired a financial advisor before the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在并购前聘请了一位理财顾问。
senses.why: The root means to cause someone to see, so an advisor is literally the person who makes the situation visible to you.
senses.whyCN: 词根的意思是「使人看见」，所以 advisor 字面上就是那个让你看清局面的人——你看不到的风险，他替你看。

senses.title: A teacher who guides a student’s studies
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or college who helps students choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里帮助学生选课、规划学业的教师
senses.example: My advisor suggested I take statistics in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 我的导师建议我第二年修统计学。
senses.why: The same seeing image narrows to one field: the advisor sees the whole curriculum and points out the path a student cannot yet see.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「看清」的意象收窄到学业这一域：导师看得见整张课程地图，于是指出学生自己还看不见的那条路。

senses.title: A senior official who advises a government
senses.definition: a senior official who gives advice to a government or a head of state, often in a titled post
senses.definitionCN: 向政府或国家元首提供意见的高级官员，常带正式头衔
senses.example: He served as national security advisor for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 他担任了四年国家安全顾问。
senses.why: Here the seeing is done for a whole state: the advisor is the extra pair of eyes attached to power, which is why the spelling advisor is preferred in official titles.
senses.whyCN: 这里是替整个国家「看」：顾问是接在权力旁边的另一双眼睛，也正因这种正式色彩，官方头衔更偏爱 advisor 这一拼写。

intro.en: Advisor is built on the Latin verb for seeing: advice began as making something visible to another person.
intro.cn: advisor 建立在拉丁语表示「看」的动词上：建议最初就是把事情让别人看见。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visum supplied the stem for vision, visible and advise.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其过去分词 visum 提供了 vision、visible 与 advise 的词干。

items.en: Vulgar Latin advisare combined ad-, toward, with visum, giving the sense to cause to see or to consider.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 advisare 由 ad-「向」与 visum 组合，义为「使看见、使考虑」。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to perceive, to consider and to give an opinion, and it carried the word north.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察觉、考虑、发表意见」，并把这个词向北传播。

items.en: Middle English avisen meant to consider or to counsel, and the noun advice grew beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语 avisen 意为「考虑、劝告」，名词 advice 随之产生。

items.en: Adviser is advise plus the agent suffix -er; advisor is a later variant spelling, now common in American official titles.
items.cn: adviser 由 advise 加施事后缀 -er 构成；advisor 是后起的异形拼写，如今常见于美式官方头衔。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the see family; the near-meaning group lists other people you pay to think for you.
note.cn: 形近组留在「看」这一词族内；近义组列出其他受聘替你思考的人。

entries.definition: The usual British spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式常用拼写。

entries.definition: To give someone an opinion about what they should do.
entries.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做给出意见。

entries.definition: Worth doing; sensible under the circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 值得做的；在当时情况下明智的。

entries.definition: An expert paid to give professional advice, often from outside the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 受聘提供专业意见的专家，常来自机构外部。

entries.definition: A person trained to give guidance, especially on personal or legal matters.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、提供指导的人，尤指个人或法律事务。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides a less experienced one over time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期指导经验较少者的资深人士。

normalIntro.en: Remember advisor through advise: the advisor is the one who does the advising.
normalIntro.cn: 用 advise 记 advisor：advisor 就是做 advise 这件事的人。

normal.en: Advise plus -er equals the person who advises, exactly like teach plus -er gives teacher.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er 就是提建议的人，正如 teach 加 -er 得到 teacher。

normal.en: The vis inside advisor is the same vis in vision and visible: an advisor gives you vision.
normal.cn: advisor 里的 vis 与 vision、visible 中的 vis 相同：顾问给你视野。

normal.en: Split it as ad plus visor: a visor is what you look through, and an advisor is who you look through.
normal.cn: 拆成 ad 加 visor：visor 是你透过它看的东西，advisor 是你透过他看的人。

normal.en: Advisor ends in -or like doctor and professor, which is why official titles prefer it.
normal.cn: advisor 以 -or 结尾，像 doctor、professor，所以正式头衔偏爱这种拼写。

normal.en: Advice is the thing, advisor is the person; one is uncountable, the other can be counted.
normal.cn: advice 是东西，advisor 是人；前者不可数，后者可数。

abstract.en: Picture a foggy road and a person walking beside you holding a lamp: that lamp is the advice.
abstract.cn: 想象一条雾中的路，旁边有人提着一盏灯：那盏灯就是建议。

abstract.en: Imagine a map you cannot read, and a finger tracing the route for you.
abstract.cn: 想象一张你读不懂的地图，一根手指替你描出路线。

abstract.en: Think of a second pair of eyes borrowed for a decision you must make alone.
abstract.cn: 想象为一个必须独自做出的决定借来的第二双眼睛。

examples.en: Every freshman is assigned an advisor at the start of the term.
examples.cn: 每位新生在学期开始时都会被分配一位指导教师。

examples.en: The advisor warned that the investment carried serious risks.
examples.cn: 顾问警告说这项投资带有严重风险。

examples.en: She works as a legal advisor to several small charities.
examples.cn: 她担任几家小型慈善机构的法律顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额的歪泽」——额（ad）头一歪，泽（visor）出一双眼睛替你看路，这人就是顾问。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 visum（videre「看」的过去分词）构成通俗拉丁语 advisare「使看见、使考虑」，经古法语 aviser 进入英语 advise，再加施事后缀 -er／-or 构成「出主意的人」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep one image: someone else sees the situation clearly and tells you what to do, whether about money, courses or state affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保留同一意象：别人把局面看清，再告诉你怎么做——无论是钱、课程还是国家大事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pair of eyes that makes the situation visible
core.cn: 核心意象：让局面变得可见的第二双眼睛

branches.en: Seeing done as a paid profession.
branches.cn: 把「看清」当成受聘的职业。

branches.en: Seeing narrowed to a curriculum.
branches.cn: 把「看清」收窄到课程地图。

branches.en: Seeing attached to state power.
branches.cn: 把「看清」接到国家权力旁边。

branches.en: Both give a recommendation, not an order.
branches.cn: 两者给的都是建议，不是命令。

branches.en: Both are formal posts with a title.
branches.cn: 两者都是带正式头衔的职位。

intro.en: Advisor is a transparent Latin build: a prefix of direction, a root of sight, and a suffix that turns an action into a person.
intro.cn: advisor 是透明的拉丁语构词：一个方向前缀、一个视觉词根，再加一个把动作变成人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus visum produced advisare; English kept the verb advise and built the agent noun on top of it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 visum 产生 advisare；英语保留动词 advise，并在其上构成施事名词。

latinEntries.example: Videre is the source of vis-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: videre 是 vis- 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Visum supplied the stem of advisare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: visum 提供了 advisare 的词干。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to see, to consider
latinEntries.example: Advisare became Old French aviser.
latinEntries.exampleCN: advisare 变成古法语 aviser。

definition_zh: 提倡；主张；拥护者；倡导者；辩护律师
definition_en: to publicly support a cause or policy, or a person who speaks in support of one, especially a lawyer
core_image: 一个人站在人群前，把手高高举起，替无声者说话
scene: 社区里有人担心老图书馆会被拆掉，居民们推选出一位代表。She became an advocate for the old library and spoke at every meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 advocate 是名词「拥护者、倡导者」（第 2 个义项：公开支持某事业的人）；句意为她成了老图书馆的倡导者，并在每次会上发言。

pos.zh: 拥护者；倡导者；辩护律师

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -acy 构成，义为「倡导；拥护」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「提倡者」，较罕见
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「倡导的」，较罕见

senses.title: To publicly support a cause or policy
senses.definition: to speak or act publicly in support of a cause, policy, or group
senses.definitionCN: 公开以言语或行动支持某项事业、政策或群体
senses.example: Several doctors advocate a shorter working week.
senses.exampleCN: 几位医生主张缩短每周工作时间。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to call someone to one's aid, so advocating is calling support toward a cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「召人来帮忙」，所以提倡就是把支持召唤到某项事业上。

senses.title: A person who supports a cause
senses.definition: a person who publicly speaks or works for a cause or for the interests of a group
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某项事业或某群体利益发声、奔走的人
senses.example: She became an advocate for the old library and spoke at every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了老图书馆的倡导者，并在每次会上发言。
senses.why: The noun is the person who has been called, or who calls others, to the aid of a cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指被召唤来、或召唤他人来支援某项事业的人。

senses.title: A lawyer who speaks for a client
senses.definition: a lawyer who pleads a client's case, especially in some legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 为当事人辩护的律师，尤用于某些法律体系
senses.example: The advocate rose to address the court.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师起身向法庭陈词。
senses.why: In law the advocate is literally the one called to a person's side to speak for them.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，辩护律师字面上就是被召到当事人身旁替其说话的人。

intro.en: Advocate comes from a Latin verb meaning to call someone to one's aid.
intro.cn: advocate 出自一个意为「召人来帮忙」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤、召唤。

items.en: Ad- plus vocare gave 'to call to one's aid or support'.
items.cn: ad- 加 vocare 构成「召来相助或支持」。

items.en: Advocatus named a person called to help, especially in legal matters.
items.cn: advocatus 指被召来帮忙的人，尤指法律事务中的人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun and its legal sense toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词及其法律义带入英语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal sense narrowed, while the general sense of public support widened.
items.cn: 法律义收窄，而公开支持的一般义扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'call to aid' root; the near-meaning group gathers supporters and legal speakers.
note.cn: 形近组共享「召来相助」词根；近义组收支持者与法律代言人。

entries.definition: Public support for a cause or policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡导；拥护」，由本词加 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: A person who advocates; rarer than advocate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提倡者」，比 advocate 更少见。

entries.definition: Relating to advocacy; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倡导的」，较罕见。

entries.definition: A hobby or secondary occupation; from the same verb of calling away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「业余爱好」，出自同一「召唤」动词，但语义分叉不同。

entries.definition: A person who backs a person, team, or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者」，范围最广。

entries.definition: A person who actively defends a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「捍卫者；为……而战」，语气更强。

entries.definition: A person who helps something become accepted or successful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推动者、发起人」，侧重促成。

entries.definition: A person trained to advise clients and represent them in law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「律师」，对应法律义项的上位词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the 'call to aid' root from a courtroom to a community meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「召来相助」词根，从法庭走到社区会议。

normal.en: Vocare means to call, so an advocate is someone called to help a cause.
normal.cn: vocare 意为召唤，所以 advocate 就是被召来帮助某项事业的人。

normal.en: Advocacy is the noun for the activity of advocating.
normal.cn: advocacy 是表示「倡导活动」的名词。

normal.en: A lawyer is called to a client's side, which is why advocate also means lawyer.
normal.cn: 律师被召到当事人身旁，所以 advocate 也指律师。

normal.en: Advocate for a cause is the modern way to say speak up for it.
normal.cn: advocate for a cause 是「为某项事业发声」的现代说法。

normal.en: A devil's advocate argues the other side just to test an idea.
normal.cn: devil's advocate 指为了检验观点而故意唱反调的人。

abstract.en: A figure standing in front of a crowd, one hand raised.
abstract.cn: 一个人站在人群前，举起一只手。

abstract.en: A voice lent to someone who has none.
abstract.cn: 把声音借给没有声音的人。

abstract.en: A chair pulled up beside the accused in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 法庭上，一把椅子被拉到被告身旁。

examples.en: The group advocates cleaner public transport.
examples.cn: 这个团体主张更清洁的公共交通。

examples.en: She is a strong advocate of free education.
examples.cn: 她是免费教育的坚定拥护者。

examples.en: The advocate presented the client's case calmly.
examples.cn: 辩护律师冷静地陈述了当事人的案情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃凯特」——阿德把大家召来，为无声者说话

root: 源自拉丁语 advocatus「被召来相助的人」，出自 advocare「召来相助」，由 ad-「向」加 vocare「召唤」构成；古法语 avocat 带入英语。核心是「被召到某人身边替他说话」，由此发展出「提倡、主张」「拥护者、倡导者」与「辩护律师」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: publicly supporting a cause, the person who supports it, and the lawyer who speaks for a client.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：公开支持某项事业、支持该事业的人、替当事人说话的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stands before a crowd with one hand raised, speaking for the voiceless.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在人群前举手，替无声者说话。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: support is called toward a policy or group.
branches.cn: 事业线：支持被召唤到某项政策或群体上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who answers the call and speaks.
branches.cn: 人物线：回应召唤并开口说话的人。

branches.en: THE COURT: a lawyer is called to a client's side.
branches.cn: 法庭线：律师被召到当事人身旁。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the cause and its supporter share one act of speaking up.
branches.cn: 声音线：事业与支持者共享同一个「发声」动作。

branches.en: THE ROLE: supporter and lawyer are both called to help another.
branches.cn: 角色线：支持者与律师都是被召来帮助他人的。

intro.en: Advocate is a Latin verb of calling, with a person suffix and English endings around it.
intro.cn: advocate 是一个表示「召唤」的拉丁动词，带表示人的后缀，并加上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, advocare and advocatus are recorded, so the family is well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare、advocare 与 advocatus 均有记录，词族文献充分。

items.example: It directs the calling toward someone.
It is the direct source of advocate.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advocate 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks both noun and verb uses in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中同时标出名词与动词用法。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -acy 构成，义为「倡导；拥护」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「提倡者」，较罕见
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「倡导的」，较罕见

definition_zh: 提倡者；拥护者；（苏格兰法）出庭辩护人
definition_en: a person who publicly supports a cause or policy; in Scots law, a pleader admitted to practise before the higher courts
core_image: 被叫到你身边、替你出声的那个人
scene: 会场后排有人站起来，一遍遍替那条提案说话。He was a lifelong advocator of free public libraries.
sceneCN: 这里 advocator 是「提倡者」（第 1 个义项：公开支持某项事业或主张的人）；句意为他一生都是免费公共图书馆的提倡者。核心画面是有人被叫到你身边替你出声。

collocations.phrase: advocator for the rights of children
become an advocator of the plan

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「提倡；拥护」，读作 /ˈædvəkeɪt/
加 -acy 构成，义为「拥护；提倡；辩护」
加 -ation 构成，义为「召唤到旁；辩护」，今较罕见

senses.title: A person who publicly supports a cause
senses.definition: a person who argues in favour of a policy, idea or group, often repeatedly and in public
senses.definitionCN: 为某项政策、理念或群体辩护的人，常反复且公开地表态
senses.example: She is an outspoken advocator of prison reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她是监狱改革直言不讳的提倡者。
senses.why: Advocare means to call someone to your side, so an advocator is the voice you have summoned to speak for a cause.
senses.whyCN: advocare 意为「把某人叫到身边」，所以 advocator 就是你为一项事业召来的那个声音——他替你开口。

senses.title: A pleader in Scots law
senses.definition: in Scots law, a lawyer admitted to plead before the higher courts, a member of the Faculty of Advocates
senses.definitionCN: 在苏格兰法中，获准在高等法院出庭辩护的律师，即律师公会成员
senses.example: The advocator addressed the court on a point of procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 那位辩护人就一项程序问题向法庭陈述。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense and the closest to the Latin: the advocatus was literally the friend called into court to stand beside the accused.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也最贴近拉丁语：advocatus 字面上就是被叫进法庭、站在被告身旁的朋友。

intro.en: Advocator comes from calling, not from seeing: Latin vocare, to call, is the engine of the whole family.
intro.cn: advocator 来自「叫」，不是「看」：拉丁语 vocare「呼叫」是整个词族的引擎。

items.en: Vocare meant to call, and it also gave English voice, vocal, vocabulary and invoke.
items.cn: vocare 意为「呼叫」，它也给了英语 voice、vocal、vocabulary 与 invoke。

items.en: Advocare joined ad-, to, with vocare, meaning to call someone to one’s aid, especially in court.
items.cn: advocare 把 ad-「向」与 vocare 结合，义为「召人来相助」，尤指法庭上。

items.en: Advocatus was the person so called: a legal helper or friend who stood beside a party in a suit.
items.cn: advocatus 就是被召来的人：在诉讼中站在当事人身旁的法律帮手或朋友。

items.en: Old French avocat carried the legal sense into medieval Europe and later into English advocate.
items.cn: 古法语 avocat 把法律义带入中世纪欧洲，后来进入英语 advocate。

items.en: Advocator is advocate plus the agent suffix -or; it survives mainly in Scots law and in formal prose, while advocate is the everyday noun.
items.cn: advocator 由 advocate 加施事后缀 -or 构成；它主要存留于苏格兰法与正式文体，日常名词用 advocate。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about avocation, which looks related but means a hobby; the near-meaning group lists other public supporters.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 avocation 看似同族却指「爱好」；近义组列出其他公开支持者。

entries.definition: The everyday noun and verb for a public supporter.
entries.definitionCN: 表示公开支持者的常用名词与动词。

entries.definition: The activity of arguing for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项事业辩护的活动。

entries.definition: A hobby, from a- meaning away plus vocare, so calling away from work.
entries.definitionCN: 爱好，源自 a-「离开」加 vocare，即把工作叫开。

entries.definition: A person who argues in favour of a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项提议辩护的人。

entries.definition: A person who fights or argues for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项事业奋战或辩护的人。

entries.definition: A person who approves of and backs a person or idea.
entries.definitionCN: 赞同并支持某人或某理念的人。

normalIntro.en: Hear the call inside advocator: voc is the same voc as voice and vocal.
normalIntro.cn: 听出 advocator 里的「叫」：voc 与 voice、vocal 中的 voc 相同。

normal.en: Ad plus voc plus -ator: the one called to your side to speak.
normal.cn: ad 加 voc 加 -ator：被叫到你身边替你说话的人。

normal.en: Vocare means to call, so advocator is a caller-for, not a looker-on.
normal.cn: vocare 意为「呼叫」，所以 advocator 是替人喊话的人，不是旁观者。

normal.en: Advocator and advocate share a stem; the -or ending only makes it sound more formal.
normal.cn: advocator 与 advocate 同干；-or 结尾只是让它听起来更正式。

normal.en: Do not confuse advocacy with avocation: one is arguing for a cause, the other is a hobby.
normal.cn: 别把 advocacy 与 avocation 弄混：前者为事业辩护，后者是爱好。

normal.en: In court the advocator stands beside you, which is exactly what ad- plus vocare describes.
normal.cn: 法庭上 advocator 站在你身旁，这正是 ad- 加 vocare 描述的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a silent defendant and a friend summoned to speak in his place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉默的被告，和一位被召来替他说话的朋友。

abstract.en: Imagine a cause with no voice until someone is called to lend it one.
abstract.cn: 想象一项事业本无声，直到有人被召来借给它一个声音。

abstract.en: Think of a megaphone handed to the person who believes in the idea most.
abstract.cn: 想象把扩音器递给最相信这个理念的人。

examples.en: He was remembered as an advocator of universal education.
examples.cn: 人们记得他是普及教育的提倡者。

examples.en: The advocator rose and addressed the bench without notes.
examples.cn: 辩护人起身，不用讲稿向法官席陈述。

examples.en: Few advocators of the policy remained after the scandal.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后，这项政策的拥护者所剩无几。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱的我凯特」——爱（ad）我（vo）凯（ca）特（tor），爱我的人被叫来替我说话，就是提倡者、辩护人。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 vocare「呼叫」构成 advocare「召来相助」，其过去分词 advocatus 指「被召到身旁的人」，经古法语 avocat 进入英语，加 -or 成 advocator。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses keep the image of a voice summoned to stand beside someone: for a cause in public, or for a client in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留「被召来站在某人身旁的声音」这一意象：在公开场合为事业，或在法庭上为当事人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice called to stand beside you
core.cn: 核心意象：被叫来站在你身旁的声音

branches.en: The voice speaks for an idea.
branches.cn: 这个声音为理念说话。

branches.en: The voice speaks for a client in court.
branches.cn: 这个声音在法庭上为当事人说话。

branches.en: Both are summoned rather than self-appointed.
branches.cn: 两者都是被召来，而非自封。

branches.en: Support repeated in public over years.
branches.cn: 多年在公开场合反复支持。

branches.en: Support formalized as a legal qualification.
branches.cn: 支持被制度化为一种法律资格。

intro.en: The family is built on vocare, to call, so every relative keeps the idea of a voice being summoned.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在 vocare「呼叫」上，所以每个亲属词都保留「声音被召来」的想法。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus vocare gave advocare and advocatus; English borrowed the stem twice, as advocate and as advocator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 vocare 产生 advocare 与 advocatus；英语两次借用这个词干，成为 advocate 与 advocator。

latinEntries.example: Vocare is the root of advocate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vocare 是 advocate 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Advocare was used of legal help.
latinEntries.exampleCN: advocare 用于法律相助。

latinEntries.example: Advocatus became Old French avocat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: advocatus 变成古法语 avocat。

definition_zh: 通气；曝气；充气（使空气或气体进入土壤、液体）
definition_en: the process of exposing something to air or of dissolving a gas into a liquid, so that soil, water or a drink takes in air
core_image: 把空气放进原本闷住的东西里
scene: 草坪踩得发硬，园丁推着带齿的滚筒来回走了一遍。Aeration lets the roots breathe again.
sceneCN: 这里 aeration 是「通气」（第 1 个义项：让空气进入土壤或水体）；句意为通气让根部重新呼吸。核心画面是把空气放进原本闷住的东西里。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 的动词，义为「使通气；充气于」
过去分词作形容词，义为「充了气的；曝气的」
加 -or 构成，义为「曝气器；通气装置」

senses.title: Letting air reach soil or water
senses.definition: the process of making air available to soil, roots or water, so that oxygen can reach them
senses.definitionCN: 让空气进入土壤、根部或水体的过程，使氧气能够抵达
senses.example: Regular aeration prevents the pond from turning stagnant.
senses.exampleCN: 定期曝气可防止池塘变成死水。
senses.why: Aer means air, and the suffix -ation names a process, so aeration is simply the act of putting air where it was missing.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，后缀 -ation 表示过程，所以 aeration 就是把空气放到原本缺空气的地方这一动作。

senses.title: Dissolving gas into a drink
senses.definition: the process of charging a liquid with a gas, especially carbon dioxide, to make it fizzy
senses.definitionCN: 把气体（尤指二氧化碳）压入液体使其起泡的过程
senses.example: The aeration of the water gives it a sharp bite.
senses.exampleCN: 水的充气处理让它带上刺激的口感。
senses.why: The same putting-air-in image moves from soil to liquid: here the air is forced in under pressure and stays as bubbles.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「把空气放进去」的意象从土壤移到液体：这里空气在压力下被强行压入，并以气泡形式留下。

intro.en: Aeration is air turned into a process noun: the Greek and Latin word for air plus the suffix that names an action.
intro.cn: aeration 是把「空气」变成过程名词：希腊语与拉丁语的「空气」加上表示动作的后缀。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or mist, and it is the source of the aero- prefix used across science.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、雾气」，是科学术语中 aero- 前缀的来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer with the same meaning, and it declined as aeris, giving the stem aer-.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer，意义相同，其属格为 aeris，提供词干 aer-。

items.en: Scholarly Latin aerare meant to expose to the air, built directly on the noun aer.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 aerare 意为「暴露于空气」，直接建立在名词 aer 上。

items.en: French aération named the process of airing, and English took the word in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aération 表示透气的过程，英语在十六世纪借入该词。

items.en: English aeration now covers lawn care, sewage treatment and fizzy drinks alike, all sharing one idea of air entering.
items.cn: 现代英语 aeration 同时涵盖草坪养护、污水处理与碳酸饮料，都共享「空气进入」这一想法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the aero- family; the near-meaning group lists other ways of saying that air or gas is being added.
note.cn: 形近组留在 aero- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「加入空气或气体」的说法。

entries.definition: To expose to air or to charge with gas.
entries.definitionCN: 使通气或充气于。

entries.definition: Existing or happening in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于空气中或在空中发生的。

entries.definition: Exercise that keeps the body supplied with oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 让身体持续获得氧气的运动。

entries.definition: The movement of fresh air through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 新鲜空气在空间中的流通。

entries.definition: The addition of oxygen to something.
entries.definitionCN: 向某物加入氧气。

entries.definition: The dissolving of carbon dioxide in a drink.
entries.definitionCN: 把二氧化碳溶入饮料。

normalIntro.en: Aeration is aer, air, plus -ation, a process: the process of adding air.
normalIntro.cn: aeration 就是 aer「空气」加 -ation「过程」：加空气的过程。

normal.en: Aerate plus -ion equals aeration, like operate plus -ion gives operation.
normal.cn: aerate 加 -ion 等于 aeration，正如 operate 加 -ion 得到 operation。

normal.en: Aero- always means air: aeroplane, aerosol, aeration all put air first.
normal.cn: aero- 永远表示空气：aeroplane、aerosol、aeration 都把空气放在前面。

normal.en: Think of a lawn spike: each hole is a tiny door for air, and all the holes together are aeration.
normal.cn: 想象草坪打孔器：每个孔都是空气的小门，所有孔合起来就是 aeration。

normal.en: Aerated water is fizzy water; aeration is what made it fizzy.
normal.cn: aerated water 是气泡水；aeration 就是让它起泡的那一步。

normal.en: The word is uncountable in most uses, so say aeration, not an aeration.
normal.cn: 这个词多数用法不可数，所以说 aeration，不说 an aeration。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed jar of soil and a needle that lets the sky in.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐密封的土，和一根让天空进来的针。

abstract.en: Imagine a pond holding its breath until a pump starts stirring.
abstract.cn: 想象一口池塘屏住呼吸，直到水泵开始搅动。

abstract.en: Think of bubbles as small parcels of air delivered into a liquid.
abstract.cn: 把气泡想成送进液体里的一小包空气。

examples.en: Aeration of the compacted soil took the gardener a whole afternoon.
examples.cn: 给板结的土壤通气花了园丁整整一个下午。

examples.en: The treatment plant uses aeration to break down waste.
examples.cn: 处理厂用曝气来分解废物。

examples.en: Gentle aeration improves the texture of the batter.
examples.cn: 轻度充气能改善面糊的质地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿瑞神」——爱（ae）儿（ra）瑞（tion）神，把空气这位神请进土里水里，就是通气、曝气。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」经拉丁语 aer（属格 aeris）进入学术拉丁语 aerare「使暴露于空气」，加过程后缀 -ation 构成 aeration，字面即「空气进入的过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one action seen in two places: air is let into soil or water, or pushed into a drink, and the thing that was sealed becomes open.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一动作出现在两处：空气被放进土壤或水体，或被压入饮料，原本闷住的东西变得通畅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air put into something that was sealed
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气放进原本闷住的东西

branches.en: Air reaching roots through holes.
branches.cn: 空气经孔洞抵达根部。

branches.en: Air stirred into standing water.
branches.cn: 空气被搅入静止的水体。

branches.en: Gas forced into liquid under pressure.
branches.cn: 气体在压力下压入液体。

branches.en: Both end with something no longer sealed.
branches.cn: 两者都以「不再闷住」收尾。

branches.en: The added gas stays as visible bubbles.
branches.cn: 加入的气体以可见气泡留下。

intro.en: Aeration belongs to the large aero- family, where the root always means air and the suffix decides the part of speech.
intro.cn: aeration 属于庞大的 aero- 词族，词根永远表示空气，后缀决定词性。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer passed through Latin aer and the scholarly verb aerare before English added -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aer 经拉丁语 aer 与学术动词 aerare，再由英语加上 -ation。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the root of the aero- family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是 aero- 词族的词根。

latinEntries.example: The genitive aeris gives the stem aer-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 属格 aeris 提供词干 aer-。

latinEntries.example: Aerare stands behind aerate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aerare 是 aerate 的来源。

definition_zh: 空中的；航空的；空气的；（名词）天线
definition_en: relating to the air or to aircraft, or happening high above the ground; as a noun, a device that receives radio or television signals
core_image: 悬在半空的一根细线：既是空气，也是捕捉电波的天线
scene: 清晨的山谷里，摄影师的飞行器缓缓升空，镜头俯瞰着尚未醒来的村庄。The small drone took an aerial photograph of the valley at sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 aerial 是「空中的、从空中拍摄的」（第 1 个义项：与空气或空中有关）；句意为小型无人机在日出时拍下了山谷的鸟瞰照片。画面中可辨识：飞行器、山谷、晨雾。

collocations.zh: 鸟瞰；从空中看到的景象

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 aerial 加 -ly 构成，义为「在空中；通过航空方式」
由 aerial 加 -ist 构成，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人

senses.title: Existing in or relating to the air
senses.titleCN: 空气的；存在于空气中的
senses.definition: relating to the air or existing in it
senses.definitionCN: 与空气有关或存在于空气中的
senses.example: Aerial moisture turned the morning air into a thick mist.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的水汽让清晨的空气变成了浓雾。
senses.why: Aer is the Greek word for air, and this adjective simply points to that element.
senses.whyCN: aer 是希腊语里表示「空气」的词，这个形容词直接指向这种元素。

senses.title: High above the ground
senses.titleCN: 高悬空中的；在空中发生的
senses.definition: happening or situated high above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 发生在地面上方高处的，或位于高处的
senses.example: An aerial cableway carried the tourists across the gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条空中索道把游客送过了峡谷。
senses.why: The same air becomes height: what is aerial is up there, away from the ground.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「空气」义进一步变成高度：aerial 的东西就在上方，远离地面。

senses.title: Done from or by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航空的；从飞机上进行的
senses.definition: carried out from an aircraft, especially for photography or survey
senses.definitionCN: 从飞机上实施的，尤指摄影或勘测
senses.example: Aerial surveys mapped the damage after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，航空勘测绘制了受灾范围。
senses.why: Once the word moved from air to aircraft, work done in the sky became aerial work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从「空气」转向「飞机」，在空中完成的作业就成了 aerial 的工作。

senses.title: A device that receives signals
senses.definition: a metal device, often on a roof, that sends or receives radio and television signals
senses.definitionCN: 常装在屋顶、用于收发广播和电视信号的金属装置
senses.example: He climbed onto the roof to fix the aerial.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬上屋顶去修那根天线。
senses.why: An antenna stands up in the air to catch waves, so English reused the air word for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 天线竖立在空气中捕捉电波，于是英语干脆用「空气」这个词来称呼这个物件。

senses.title: Growing above the ground: aerial roots
senses.definition: of a plant part, growing above the ground rather than in the soil
senses.definitionCN: 指植物器官长在地面之上而非土壤之中的
senses.example: Orchids use aerial roots to absorb moisture from the humid air.
senses.exampleCN: 兰花用气生根从湿润的空气中吸收水分。
senses.why: Botany keeps the literal sense: the root lives in the air, not in the soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了最字面的意思：这种根生活在空气里，而不是土壤里。

intro.en: Aerial is built on the Greek word for air and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: aerial 建立在希腊语表示「空气」的词上，经由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun aer meant 'air, mist, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 名词 aer 意为「空气、雾气、低层大气」。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer as 'air' and used it in both everyday and scientific writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer 表示「空气」，日常写作与科学写作中都在使用。

items.en: The adjective aerius meant 'of the air' and supplied the stem behind the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 aerius 意为「空气的」，为英语这个词提供了词干。

items.en: Aerial is recorded in the sixteenth century, first describing things in or of the air.
items.cn: aerial 于十六世纪见于记录，最初描述存在于空气中或与空气有关的事物。

items.en: In the twentieth century the noun aerial was applied to the antenna raised into the air for radio and television.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，名词 aerial 被用来指为收音机和电视竖在空中的天线。

note.en: The first group gathers words on the same air root or resembling aerial in spelling; the second gathers things that are airborne, overhead, or used to catch signals.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「空气」词根构成的词以及与 aerial 拼写相近的词；第二组收升空的、头顶上的或用于接收信号的事物。

entries.definition: To expose something to air or to force air into it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使暴露于空气；向……充气」，与 aerial 同出希腊语「空气」词根。

entries.definition: The nest of a bird of prey, built high on a cliff or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猛禽筑在高处岩壁上的巢」；只是拼写与 aerial 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A performer who works high above the ground, such as a trapeze artist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人，由 aerial 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: Carried in the air, or flying after leaving the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升空的；在空中的」，强调已经离开地面。

entries.definition: Above a person's head; in the sky directly above.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，只强调相对位置，不涉及航空。

entries.definition: A device that sends or receives radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天线」，与 aerial 的名词义项所指同类物件。

normalIntro.en: Aerial can be recalled through its air root, its suffix, and its everyday collocations.
normalIntro.cn: aerial 可以通过「空气」词根、后缀以及常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Aer means air and -ial makes an adjective, so aerial is simply 'of the air'.
normal.cn: aer 意为「空气」，-ial 构成形容词，aerial 就是「空气的」。

normal.en: An aerial view is a view from the air, which fixes the adjective in a familiar phrase.
normal.cn: aerial view 是「从空中看到的景象」，这个常见搭配能固定形容词义。

normal.en: The noun aerial is the antenna that stands up in the air to catch waves.
normal.cn: 名词 aerial 就是竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

normal.en: Aerialist adds -ist to the same word and names a person who performs in the air.
normal.cn: aerialist 加 -ist，指在空中表演的人。

normal.en: Aerate and aerobic share the same air root, so the family can be learned together.
normal.cn: aerate 与 aerobic 共享同一「空气」词根，可以整族一起记。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire hanging above a valley, catching mist on one side and signals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线悬在山谷上方，一边接住雾气，一边接收信号。

abstract.en: Think of a camera lifting off the ground: the higher it goes, the more the view deserves the name aerial.
abstract.cn: 想象相机离开地面升空：升得越高，眼前的景象越配得上 aerial 这个名字。

abstract.en: Link the word to wind on your face: air is the element behind every sense.
abstract.cn: 把这个词和风吹在脸上的感觉联系起来：空气是它所有义项背后的元素。

examples.en: The drone captured an aerial view of the flooded valley.
examples.cn: 无人机拍下了被洪水淹没的山谷鸟瞰图。

examples.en: He replaced the rusty television aerial on the roof.
examples.cn: 他更换了屋顶上生锈的电视天线。

examples.en: From the ridge, the village looked like a patch of colour in a green sea.
examples.cn: 从山脊望去，村庄像绿色海洋中的一小片色彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱瑞尔」——爱（ai）上空气，瑞（ri）尔（al）把它挂在高处，正好是悬在半空的细线。

root: 希腊语 aēr（转写为 aer）意为「空气」，拉丁语 aerius 是其形容词形式「空气的」，英语 aerial 由此而来，后缀 -ial 表示「与……有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from the element air, rise into the sky, move to aircraft, and end with two concrete objects: the antenna and the air root.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「空气」这一元素出发，升到空中，转向航空，最后落到两个具体物件：天线与气生根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line suspended in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根悬在空中的细线

branches.en: The literal element: what belongs to the air.
branches.cn: 本义：属于空气的事物。

branches.en: Height above the ground, where the air is.
branches.cn: 高度：位于地面之上的空中。

branches.en: Work done from aircraft in the sky.
branches.cn: 从飞机上进行的作业。

branches.en: The antenna that stands in the air to catch waves.
branches.cn: 竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

branches.en: The plant root that lives in humid air.
branches.cn: 生长在湿润空气中的植物根。

intro.en: Aerial is built from a Greek air root plus a Latin adjective ending, and its family is easy to map.
intro.cn: aerial 由希腊语「空气」词根加拉丁语形容词词尾构成，词族容易梳理。

latinIntro.en: Latin took aer from Greek and formed aerius 'of the air'; English borrowed the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 aer，并构成 aerius「空气的」；英语借用了这个形容词。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the source of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是整个词族的来源。

latinEntries.example: Aerius became aerial in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aerius 在英语中变成了 aerial。

definition_zh: 有氧的（运动）；需氧的（生物）；靠氧气供能的
definition_en: using oxygen to produce energy over a sustained period; of organisms, requiring oxygen to live; of exercise, strengthening the heart and lungs
core_image: 一边呼吸一边持续燃烧，氧气始终供得上
scene: 跑道上的呼吸声很稳，脚步没有停下来的意思。Aerobic training keeps the heart working for a long time.
sceneCN: 这里 aerobic 是「有氧的」（第 1 个义项：靠氧气持续供能、能长时间维持的运动）；句意为有氧训练让心脏长时间持续工作。核心画面是氧气始终供得上的持续燃烧。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ally 构成，义为「以有氧方式」
加 -s 构成，义为「有氧健身操；有氧运动」
加否定前缀 an- 构成，义为「无氧的；厌氧的」

senses.title: Of exercise, sustained by oxygen
senses.definition: of physical activity that is steady enough for the body to supply oxygen continuously, strengthening heart and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 指强度平稳、身体能持续供氧的体育活动，可增强心肺功能
senses.example: Swimming is one of the best aerobic activities.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳是最好的有氧活动之一。
senses.why: Aer means air and bios means life, so aerobic literally describes life kept going by air: effort you can sustain because breathing keeps up.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，bios 意为「生命」，所以 aerobic 字面就是「靠空气维持的生命」：因为呼吸跟得上，这份用力才能持续。

senses.title: Of organisms, needing oxygen to live
senses.definition: of bacteria or other organisms that can live and grow only in the presence of oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 指只有在有氧环境中才能生存繁殖的细菌或其他生物
senses.example: Aerobic bacteria break down the waste in the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 需氧菌分解池中的废物。
senses.why: This is the older scientific sense from Pasteur: the same air-plus-life image applied to a microbe rather than to a runner.
senses.whyCN: 这是来自巴斯德的更早的科学义项：同一个「空气加生命」的意象用在微生物身上，而不是跑者身上。

intro.en: Aerobic was coined for microbiology before it ever reached the gym: air plus life, written in Greek.
intro.cn: aerobic 先为微生物学而造，之后才走进健身房：空气加生命，用希腊语写成。

items.en: Greek aer meant air, the first half of the compound.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」，是复合词的前半。

items.en: Greek bios meant life, and it also gives biology, biography and biosphere.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，它也给出 biology、biography 与 biosphere。

items.en: Pasteur used French aérobie in the eighteen sixties for microbes that need free oxygen.
items.cn: 巴斯德在十九世纪六十年代用法语 aérobie 指需要游离氧的微生物。

items.en: English aerobic appeared in the eighteen seventies as the adjective of aerobe, first in biology.
items.cn: 英语 aerobic 于十九世纪七十年代作为 aerobe 的形容词出现，最初用于生物学。

items.en: In the nineteen sixties the word moved into exercise science, naming effort that oxygen can sustain.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代该词进入运动科学，指氧气能够支撑的运动强度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the aero- family and its opposite; the near-meaning group lists words used for the same kind of training.
note.cn: 形近组收 aero- 词族及其反面；近义组收描述同类训练的词语。

entries.definition: Without oxygen; the an- prefix negates aer-.
entries.definitionCN: 无氧的；an- 前缀否定 aer-。

entries.definition: A class or system of aerobic exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 有氧健身操课程或有氧运动体系。

entries.definition: In the air; sharing aer- but not bios.
entries.definitionCN: 在空中的；共享 aer- 但不含 bios。

entries.definition: Relating to heart and blood vessels, often used of the same training.
entries.definitionCN: 与心脏和血管有关的，常指同一类训练。

entries.definition: The ability to keep going for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间持续下去的能力。

entries.definition: Energetic and forceful, though not necessarily oxygen-sustained.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛而有力的，但不一定靠氧气维持。

normalIntro.en: Split aerobic into aer, air, and bic from bios, life: life that runs on air.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aerobic 拆成 aer「空气」与来自 bios「生命」的 bic：靠空气运转的生命。

normal.en: Aer plus bios plus -ic: the adjective of air-life.
normal.cn: aer 加 bios 加 -ic：空气生命的形容词。

normal.en: If you can talk while doing it, it is probably aerobic.
normal.cn: 如果做的时候还能说话，那多半是有氧的。

normal.en: Add an- and you flip it: anaerobic means the oxygen has run out.
normal.cn: 加上 an- 就翻转：anaerobic 表示氧气已跟不上。

normal.en: Aerobic bacteria need air; aerobic exercise gives you more air.
normal.cn: 需氧菌需要空气；有氧运动给你更多空气。

normal.en: The noun aerobics is just this adjective wearing an -s.
normal.cn: 名词 aerobics 就是这个形容词戴上 -s。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning steadily because the window is open.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛因窗户开着而稳定燃烧。

abstract.en: Imagine a fire that never smokes because air arrives as fast as it is used.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆从不冒烟的火，因为空气抵达的速度与消耗一样快。

abstract.en: Think of a runner and a microbe sharing one rule: no air, no life.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者与微生物共享一条规则：没有空气，就没有生命。

examples.en: Doctors recommend thirty minutes of aerobic exercise most days.
examples.cn: 医生建议大多数日子进行三十分钟有氧运动。

examples.en: The test measures aerobic capacity on a treadmill.
examples.cn: 该测试在跑步机上测量有氧能力。

examples.en: Aerobic organisms cannot survive in the sealed layer of mud.
examples.cn: 需氧生物无法在密封的泥层中存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱肉比克」——爱（ae）肉（ro）比（bi）克（c），爱跑步的肉体靠氧气比拼耐力，就是有氧的。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 bios「生命」构成 aerobic，字面为「靠空气而活的」；十九世纪先用于微生物学，二十世纪转入运动科学，指氧气能持续支撑的强度。

sensesIntro.en: One image covers both senses: life kept going by a steady supply of air, whether in a working muscle or in a bacterium.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个意象覆盖两个义项：靠稳定供气维持的生命，无论是在工作的肌肉里，还是在细菌里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life sustained by a steady supply of air
core.cn: 核心意象：靠稳定供气维持的生命

branches.en: Muscle burning fuel with enough oxygen.
branches.cn: 肌肉在氧气充足下燃烧燃料。

branches.en: A microbe that lives only with oxygen.
branches.cn: 只有在有氧时才存活的微生物。

branches.en: Both stop when the air stops.
branches.cn: 两者都在断气时停下。

branches.en: Effort paced so breathing keeps up.
branches.cn: 把强度控制在呼吸跟得上的节奏。

branches.en: The opposite is named by adding an-.
branches.cn: 反面由加 an- 来命名。

intro.en: Aerobic is a two-root Greek compound, so its relatives are built by swapping either root or by adding a negating prefix.
intro.cn: aerobic 是双词根的希腊语复合词，因此其亲属词通过替换任一词根或加否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer and bios travelled through French aérobie into English; Latin had no part in this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aer 与 bios 经法语 aérobie 进入英语；这个复合词与拉丁语无关。

definition_zh: 有氧健身操；有氧运动（复数形式，常作单数用）
definition_en: a system of physical exercise done to music, or any sustained activity that improves the body’s use of oxygen; a plural noun usually treated as singular
core_image: 一群人跟着节拍持续动，呼吸始终跟得上
scene: 镜墙前音乐一响，整排人同时抬起膝盖。Aerobics is her favourite part of the week.
sceneCN: 这里 aerobics 是「有氧健身操」（第 1 个义项：配乐的集体健身课程）；句意为有氧操是她一周中最喜欢的部分。核心画面是一群人跟着节拍持续动而呼吸跟得上。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -s 的形容词，义为「有氧的；需氧的」
加 -ally 构成，义为「以有氧方式」
加 aqua- 构成，义为「水中有氧操」

senses.title: A class of rhythmic exercise to music
senses.definition: a class in which a group performs rhythmic movements to music in order to improve fitness
senses.definitionCN: 一群人跟着音乐做有节奏动作以增强体能的课程
senses.example: She teaches aerobics at the community centre on Tuesdays.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周二在社区中心教有氧操。
senses.why: The adjective aerobic was turned into a noun by adding -s, the same ending that names activities like gymnastics and athletics.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 aerobic 加上 -s 变成名词，这个结尾与 gymnastics、athletics 一样，用来给活动命名。

senses.title: Any sustained oxygen-using exercise
senses.definition: any continuous activity, such as running or cycling, that improves how efficiently the body uses oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 任何能提升身体用氧效率的持续活动，如跑步或骑车
senses.example: Aerobics does not have to happen in a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 有氧运动不一定非要在健身房里进行。
senses.why: Here the word keeps its scientific half: the point is not the music but the steady supply of air that the effort allows.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留的是它的科学那一半：重点不在音乐，而在这份用力所允许的持续供气。

intro.en: Aerobics is a twentieth-century noun built on a nineteenth-century adjective, and it was popularized by a doctor.
intro.cn: aerobics 是二十世纪建立于十九世纪形容词之上的名词，由一位医生推广开来。

items.en: Greek aer, air, supplies the first root of the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer「空气」提供整个词族的第一个词根。

items.en: Greek bios, life, supplies the second root, as in biology.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios「生命」提供第二个词根，如 biology。

items.en: The adjective aerobic entered biology in the eighteen seventies and exercise science in the nineteen sixties.
items.cn: 形容词 aerobic 于十九世纪七十年代进入生物学，二十世纪六十年代进入运动科学。

items.en: The noun aerobics was popularized from nineteen sixty-eight by the American physician Kenneth Cooper, who used it for oxygen-using exercise.
items.cn: 名词 aerobics 自一九六八年起由美国医生肯尼斯·库珀推广，用以指利用氧气的运动。

items.en: The ending -ics names a field or activity, as in gymnastics, athletics and aerobics, and takes a singular verb.
items.cn: 结尾 -ics 用于给领域或活动命名，如 gymnastics、athletics、aerobics，并接单数动词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about aerobatic and acrobatics, which sound close but belong to flying and to tumbling; the near-meaning group lists comparable workouts.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 aerobatic 与 acrobatics 音近却分别属于飞行与翻腾；近义组列出可比的锻炼方式。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this noun was made.
entries.definitionCN: 造出这个名词的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to spectacular feats of flying, not to fitness classes.
entries.definitionCN: 与特技飞行有关，而非健身课程。

entries.definition: Gymnastic feats of balance and tumbling.
entries.definitionCN: 平衡与翻腾的体操技艺。

entries.definition: Gymnastic exercises done to build fitness and grace.
entries.definitionCN: 为增强体能与体态而做的体操练习。

entries.definition: Short for cardiovascular exercise, the same training idea.
entries.definitionCN: cardiovascular exercise 的简称，同一训练理念。

entries.definition: A session of physical exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 一次体育锻炼。

normalIntro.en: Aerobics is aerobic plus -s, the ending that turns a quality into an activity.
normalIntro.cn: aerobics 就是 aerobic 加 -s，这个结尾把性质变成活动。

normal.en: Gymnastics, athletics, aerobics: all end in -ics and all name an activity.
normal.cn: gymnastics、athletics、aerobics：都以 -ics 结尾，都指一项活动。

normal.en: Say aerobics is, not aerobics are, because the -ics noun is treated as singular.
normal.cn: 说 aerobics is，不说 aerobics are，因为 -ics 名词作单数处理。

normal.en: Aerobics keeps the air in aer-: you should still be able to breathe and talk.
normal.cn: aerobics 保留 aer- 里的空气：你应该仍能呼吸和说话。

normal.en: Do not mix aerobics with acrobatics: one is fitness, the other is flipping.
normal.cn: 别把 aerobics 与 acrobatics 弄混：前者是健身，后者是翻腾。

normal.en: Water aerobics is the same idea with the floor taken away.
normal.cn: 水中有氧操是同一理念，只是把地板抽走。

abstract.en: Picture a room breathing in time with the music.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间跟着音乐一起呼吸。

abstract.en: Imagine a heart as a pump that gets stronger the longer it is kept gently busy.
abstract.cn: 想象心脏是一台泵，被温和地持续使用越久就越强。

abstract.en: Think of a fire kept alive by a rhythm of air rather than a sudden gust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆火靠有节奏的送风而非一阵狂风维持。

examples.en: Aerobics is offered three evenings a week at the sports centre.
examples.cn: 体育中心每周三个晚上开设有氧操课。

examples.en: She switched from weights to aerobics after the injury.
examples.cn: 受伤后她从举重改为有氧操。

examples.en: The instructor made aerobics feel like a party.
examples.cn: 教练让有氧操课感觉像一场派对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱肉比克斯」——爱（ae）肉（ro）比（bi）克（c）斯（s），爱动的肉体跟着节拍比耐力，末尾的斯就是那门操课。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 bios「生命」构成形容词 aerobic，再加活动名词后缀 -ics 构成 aerobics；一九六八年后由美国医生库珀推广，指靠氧气持续供能的锻炼。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name the same kind of effort: movement steady enough that air keeps arriving, whether it is packaged as a class to music or simply as running.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项指同一类用力：平稳到空气持续抵达的运动，无论它被包装成配乐课程，还是干脆就是跑步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group moving in rhythm with breath keeping up
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人跟着节奏动而呼吸跟得上

branches.en: The activity packaged as a music class.
branches.cn: 活动被包装成配乐课程。

branches.en: The activity defined by oxygen use alone.
branches.cn: 活动仅由用氧来定义。

branches.en: Both take a singular verb despite the -s.
branches.cn: 两者虽带 -s 仍接单数动词。

branches.en: A group and an instructor are implied.
branches.cn: 隐含一群人与一位教练。

branches.en: No equipment or studio is required.
branches.cn: 不需要器械或健身房。

intro.en: Aerobics shows how English names an activity: take an adjective and add -ics, exactly as gymnastics was formed.
intro.cn: aerobics 展示了英语如何给活动命名：取一个形容词加 -ics，正如 gymnastics 的构成方式。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek, aer and bios; the activity suffix -ics is also Greek in origin, so no Latin layer is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语 aer 与 bios；活动后缀 -ics 也源自希腊语，因此不涉及拉丁语层。

latinEntries.example: Aqua- gives aquaerobics.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aqua- 构成 aquaerobics。

definition_zh: 石陨石；陨石（旧称，今多用 meteorite）
definition_en: a stony meteorite; an older term for any meteorite, now largely replaced by meteorite in scientific use
core_image: 一块从天上落下来的石头
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里躺着一块黑灰色的石块，标签写得很旧。The aerolite fell in a field two centuries ago.
sceneCN: 这里 aerolite 是「石陨石」（第 1 个义项：以石质为主的陨石）；句意为这块石陨石两个世纪前落在一片田里。核心画面是一块从天上落下来的石头。

derivatives.zh: 同义异形词，末尾用 -th 而非 -te，义同为「石陨石」
加 -ic 构成，义为「陨石的；与陨石有关的」

senses.title: A stony meteorite
senses.definition: a meteorite composed mainly of silicate rock rather than metal, as opposed to a siderite
senses.definitionCN: 主要由硅酸盐岩石而非金属构成的陨石，与铁陨石相对
senses.example: The aerolite was almost entirely olivine and pyroxene.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石陨石几乎全由橄榄石与辉石构成。
senses.why: Aer means air and lithos means stone, so the word pictures a stone that arrived through the air, and the stony sense is the literal one.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，lithos 意为「石头」，所以这个词画的是「穿过空气而来的石头」，石质义正是字面义。

senses.title: Any meteorite, in older usage
senses.definition: in eighteenth and nineteenth century writing, any mass that fell from the sky, whatever its composition
senses.definitionCN: 在十八、十九世纪的文献中，泛指任何自天而降的块体，不论成分
senses.example: Early reports called every such stone an aerolite.
senses.exampleCN: 早期报道把每一块这样的石头都称作 aerolite。
senses.why: Before classification existed, the name covered the whole event of falling, so the word once meant simply a sky-stone of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 在分类学出现之前，这个名字覆盖的是「坠落」这件事本身，所以它一度只表示任何种类的天降之石。

intro.en: Aerolite is a stone named after the sky it came through: air plus stone, written in Greek.
intro.cn: aerolite 是一块以它穿过的天空命名的石头：空气加石头，用希腊语写成。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or the lower atmosphere, the same root as in aerobic.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」，与 aerobic 中的词根相同。

items.en: Greek lithos meant stone, and it gives English lithograph, monolith and Neolithic.
items.cn: 希腊语 lithos 意为「石头」，它给出英语 lithograph、monolith 与 Neolithic。

items.en: French aérolithe was formed in the eighteenth century, when falling stones were still disputed by scholars.
items.cn: 法语 aérolithe 形成于十八世纪，当时学界仍在争论天降石块是否真实。

items.en: English aerolite appeared in the same period and was the standard term for a fallen sky-stone.
items.cn: 英语 aerolite 出现于同一时期，曾是天降石块的标准称呼。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century meteorite displaced aerolite in science, leaving aerolite as a historical and literary word.
items.cn: 自十九世纪后期，meteorite 在科学中取代 aerolite，使 aerolite 成为历史与文学用词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stone and sky roots; the near-meaning group lists the modern terms for objects that fall from space.
note.cn: 形近组保留「石」与「天」两个词根；近义组列出天降物体的现代术语。

entries.definition: The same word with -th instead of -te.
entries.definitionCN: 同词异形，末尾为 -th 而非 -te。

entries.definition: A print made from a flat stone surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用平面石版印出的版画。

entries.definition: A balloon or other craft lighter than air.
entries.definitionCN: 气球或其他轻于空气的飞行器。

entries.definition: The current scientific term for a space rock that reaches the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 落到地面的太空岩石的现代科学术语。

entries.definition: A small rocky body still travelling in space.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在太空中运行的小型岩质天体。

entries.definition: An exceptionally bright meteor that often explodes.
entries.definitionCN: 极亮且常发生爆炸的流星。

normalIntro.en: Read aerolite as air-stone: aero is air and lite is lithos, stone.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aerolite 读成「空气之石」：aero 是空气，lite 是 lithos「石头」。

normal.en: Aer plus lite equals air-stone, a stone that came by air.
normal.cn: aer 加 lite 等于空气之石，一块乘空气而来的石头。

normal.en: The lite ending is the same stone as in graphite and chrysolite.
normal.cn: lite 这个词尾与 graphite、chrysolite 中的「石」相同。

normal.en: Aerolite is the old word; meteorite is the one used in papers today.
normal.cn: aerolite 是旧词；meteorite 是今天论文里用的词。

normal.en: Stony aerolite, iron siderite: the old names sorted stones by what they were made of.
normal.cn: 石质叫 aerolite，铁质叫 siderite：旧名按成分分类。

normal.en: Aerolith with -th means exactly the same thing.
normal.cn: 带 -th 的 aerolith 意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that remembers the sky it fell through.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记得自己穿过的那片天空的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a field at dawn with a black stone still warm in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明的田野，草里一块仍带余温的黑石。

abstract.en: Think of a museum label older than the science that renamed the object.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比给它改名的那门科学更旧的博物馆标签。

examples.en: The aerolite on display weighs just under two kilograms.
examples.cn: 展出的这块石陨石重不到两公斤。

examples.en: Nineteenth century letters describe the aerolite as a thunderstone.
examples.cn: 十九世纪的书信把这块陨石称作「雷石」。

examples.en: Each aerolite in the drawer was labelled with the date of its fall.
examples.cn: 抽屉里每块陨石都标注了坠落日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿罗来特」——爱（ae）儿（ro）罗（li）来（te），从天上啰啰嗦嗦落下来的那块石头，就是陨石。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 lithos「石头」构成，经法语 aérolithe 进入英语 aerolite，字面即「自空气而来的石头」；十九世纪后期在科学语境中被 meteorite 取代。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same picture at different levels of precision: a stone from the sky, first named by its stony nature and earlier by the mere fact of falling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一幅画在不同精度下的样子：一块来自天空的石头，先按石质命名，更早则仅按「坠落」这一事实命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone that arrived through the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一块穿过空气而来的石头

branches.en: The stone named by its silicate makeup.
branches.cn: 按硅酸盐成分命名的石头。

branches.en: The stone named only by its falling.
branches.cn: 仅按坠落这一事实命名的石头。

branches.en: Both keep air plus stone in the spelling.
branches.cn: 两者拼写中都保留空气加石头。

branches.en: The older, wider use before classification.
branches.cn: 分类学之前更宽的旧用法。

branches.en: Both yield to meteorite in modern science.
branches.cn: 两者在现代科学中都让位给 meteorite。

intro.en: Aerolite joins two Greek roots, so its relatives are found by following either the air root or the stone root.
intro.cn: aerolite 连接两个希腊语词根，因此沿着「空气」或「石头」任一词根都能找到它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Both roots are Greek; the word reached English through French, and no Latin layer sits between them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都是希腊语；该词经法语进入英语，中间没有拉丁语层。

definition_zh: 航空学；航空术（飞行器设计、制造与驾驶的科学）
definition_en: the science and art of designing, building and operating aircraft within the earth’s atmosphere
core_image: 把船开进空气里的那门学问
scene: 风洞的嗡鸣声里，学生盯着一组机翼数据不肯下课。Aeronautics began with balloons and ended in jets.
sceneCN: 这里 aeronautics 是「航空学」（第 1 个义项：研究大气层内飞行器设计、制造与驾驶的科学）；句意为航空学始于气球而终于喷气机。核心画面是把船开进空气里的那门学问。

derivatives.zh: 加 -al 构成，义为「航空的；航空学的」
加 -ic 构成，义同 aeronautical，较少用
去掉 -ics 构成，义为「航空者；气球驾驶者」

senses.title: The science of flight within the atmosphere
senses.definition: the branch of engineering and physics concerned with aircraft that fly inside the earth’s atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 研究与在地球大气层内飞行的飞行器有关的工程与物理分支
senses.example: She earned a doctorate in aeronautics before joining the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 她在进入实验室之前取得了航空学博士学位。
senses.why: Aer means air and nautes means sailor, so aeronautics is literally sailing in air, which is exactly how balloonists first described flight.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，nautes 意为「水手」，所以 aeronautics 字面就是「在空气中航行」，这正是早期气球驾驶者对飞行的描述。

senses.title: The practical art of flying
senses.definition: the practical skill of navigating and handling aircraft, as opposed to the theory behind them
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶与操纵飞行器的实际技艺，与其背后的理论相对
senses.example: Aeronautics in the early days was mostly courage and guesswork.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的航空术多半靠勇气与猜测。
senses.why: The sailor half of the word keeps its craft sense: a sailor is judged by handling a vessel, not by writing about it.
senses.whyCN: 词中「水手」那一半保留了技艺义：评价水手看的是操船，而不是写文章。

intro.en: Aeronautics was named when flight meant balloons: the word borrows the language of ships and lends it to the air.
intro.cn: aeronautics 得名于飞行还意味着气球的时代：这个词借来船舶的语言，再把它借给空气。

items.en: Greek aer, air, is the first root, shared with aerobic and aerolite.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer「空气」是第一个词根，与 aerobic、aerolite 共享。

items.en: Greek nautes meant sailor, from naus, ship, and it also gives nautical and astronaut.
items.cn: 希腊语 nautes 意为「水手」，源自 naus「船」，它也给出 nautical 与 astronaut。

items.en: French aéronaute was coined in the seventeen eighties for the men who ascended in the first balloons.
items.cn: 法语 aéronaute 造于十八世纪八十年代，指乘首批气球升空的人。

items.en: English aeronautics appeared in the nineteenth century as the name of the new field, on the pattern of mathematics.
items.cn: 英语 aeronautics 于十九世纪作为新学科的名称出现，构词仿照 mathematics。

items.en: In the twentieth century astronautics was formed on the same pattern for flight beyond the atmosphere, and the two are often paired.
items.cn: 二十世纪按同一模式造出 astronautics，指大气层外的飞行，两者常成对出现。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the sailor root into space and back to the sea; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring fields of flight.
note.cn: 形近组沿「水手」词根走向太空又回到海洋；近义组列出相邻的飞行领域。

entries.definition: The science of flight beyond the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层外飞行的科学。

entries.definition: A person who flies or navigates a balloon or aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶气球或飞行器的人。

entries.definition: Relating to ships and sailing on the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 与船舶和海上航行有关的。

entries.definition: The activity and industry of operating aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 运营飞行器的活动与产业。

entries.definition: The study of how air moves around solid bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 研究空气如何绕固体流动的学科。

entries.definition: The electronic systems used in aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 飞行器所用的电子系统。

normalIntro.en: Hear the sailor inside aeronautics: naut is the same naut as nautical and astronaut.
normalIntro.cn: 听出 aeronautics 里的水手：naut 与 nautical、astronaut 中的 naut 相同。

normal.en: Aer plus naut plus -ics: the field of air-sailing.
normal.cn: aer 加 naut 加 -ics：空中航行的领域。

normal.en: Astronaut is star-sailor; aeronaut is air-sailor.
normal.cn: astronaut 是星际水手；aeronaut 是空中水手。

normal.en: Aeronautics stays inside the atmosphere; astronautics leaves it.
normal.cn: aeronautics 留在大气层内；astronautics 离开它。

normal.en: The -ics ending marks a field, as in physics and mathematics.
normal.cn: -ics 结尾标记一个学科，如 physics、mathematics。

normal.en: Aeronautical is the adjective you need before engineering or university.
normal.cn: aeronautical 是放在 engineering 或 university 前的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a ship whose sea is the sky and whose hull is a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘以天空为海、以机翼为船身的船。

abstract.en: Imagine a balloonist reading the wind the way a sailor reads a current.
abstract.cn: 想象气球驾驶者像水手读洋流那样读风。

abstract.en: Think of a discipline that began with silk bags and ended with turbine blades.
abstract.cn: 想象一门始于丝绸气囊、终于涡轮叶片的学科。

examples.en: The university founded a chair of aeronautics in nineteen twenty.
examples.cn: 那所大学于一九二年设立了航空学讲席。

examples.en: Aeronautics demands both mathematics and workshop skill.
examples.cn: 航空学既要求数学，也要求车间技艺。

examples.en: His library was full of early aeronautics manuals.
examples.cn: 他的藏书室里满是早期航空学手册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱儿罗诺提克斯」——爱（aero）儿罗（nau）诺提克斯（tics），把空气当海来航行的一整套学问，就是航空学。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 nautes「水手」（源自 naus「船」）构成，经法语 aéronaute 进入英语，加学科后缀 -ics 成 aeronautics，字面即「空中航行之学」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses keep the sailor image: one is the theory of sailing in air, the other is the hands-on craft of doing it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留水手意象：一个是空中航行的理论，另一个是亲手去做的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sailing, but with air as the sea
core.cn: 核心意象：航行，只是以空气为海

branches.en: The theory of air-sailing as a discipline.
branches.cn: 空中航行作为学科的理论。

branches.en: The hands-on skill of handling craft.
branches.cn: 操纵飞行器的动手技艺。

branches.en: Both stay inside the atmosphere.
branches.cn: 两者都留在大气层内。

branches.en: The field that pairs with astronautics.
branches.cn: 与 astronautics 成对的学科。

branches.en: The craft sense inherited from sailors.
branches.cn: 从水手那里继承的技艺义。

intro.en: Aeronautics is a Greek compound plus a field suffix, and the same recipe produced astronautics a century later.
intro.cn: aeronautics 是希腊语复合词加学科后缀，同一配方在一个世纪后造出了 astronautics。

latinIntro.en: The roots aer and nautes are Greek; Latin contributed nothing to this compound, though nautical reached English via Latin nauticus.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 aer 与 nautes 都是希腊语；这个复合词没有拉丁语贡献，尽管 nautical 是经拉丁语 nauticus 进入英语的。

latinEntries.example: Avis gives aviation, a rival of aeronautics.
latinEntries.exampleCN: avis 构成 aviation，是 aeronautics 的近义竞争词。

latinEntries.example: Nauticus carried Greek nautes into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: nauticus 把希腊语 nautes 带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 飞机（英式英语）；（纸或模型）飞机
definition_en: a powered aircraft with fixed wings, called an airplane in American English, or a small model or paper copy of one
core_image: 草地上停着一架白色小飞机，机翼在阳光下投出细长的影子
scene: 第一次坐飞机的男孩把脸贴在舷窗上，看地面一点点变小。The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里的 aeroplane 是「飞机」（第 1 个义项：英式英语对固定翼航空器的称呼）；句意是飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。

pos.zh: 名词：飞机（英式）；纸飞机；飞机模型

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写变体，义为「飞机」
由希腊语「空气」与「航行」两部分构成，义为「航空学」
由「空气」与「水手」两部分构成，义为「飞艇或气球驾驶员」
由「空气」与「跑道」两部分构成，义为「小型机场」

senses.title: A fixed-wing aircraft
senses.definition: a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings, the ordinary British word for an airplane
senses.definitionCN: 有固定机翼的动力飞行器，英式英语里的常用说法
senses.example: The aeroplane climbed slowly above the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机缓缓爬升到云层之上。
senses.why: The word joins Greek aer, air, to Greek planos, wandering: a craft that wanders through the air instead of staying on a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡」合在一起：一种在空中游走、不守固定路线的机器。

senses.title: A model or paper copy
senses.definition: a small toy or folded paper object shaped like an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 做成飞机形状的小玩具或折纸物件
senses.example: He folded an aeroplane from a sheet of newspaper and threw it across the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一张报纸折了架飞机，把它扔过房间。
senses.why: Once the word names the shape rather than the machine, any small imitation of that shape can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指的是那个形状而不是那台机器时，任何模仿该形状的小物件都能用这个名字。

intro.en: A French coinage from two Greek pieces, air and wandering.
intro.cn: 一个法语新造词，由「空气」与「游荡」两个希腊部件拼成。

items.en: aer meant the lower air, the misty layer near the earth, as opposed to the clear upper sky.
items.cn: aer 指靠近地面的雾气层，即下层空气，与高处的清澈天空相对。

items.en: planos meant wandering or roaming, from the verb planasthai, to stray about.
items.cn: planos 意为「游荡的、漫游的」，来自动词 planasthai「四处游走」。

items.en: French coined aéroplane in the mid nineteenth century for an aircraft with fixed wings.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪中期造出 aéroplane，指有固定机翼的飞行器。

items.en: English borrowed the French word and used it first for early experimental flying machines.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语词，最初用来指早期的实验飞行器。

items.en: British English keeps aeroplane, while American English settled on airplane after the Wright brothers' flights.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 aeroplane，美式英语则在莱特兄弟飞行之后定下 airplane。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek element for air; the second collects the everyday words for flying machines.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「空气」的希腊成分；第二组收日常说「飞行器」的几个词。

entries.definition: the American spelling and word for the same machine
entries.definitionCN: 同一机器的美式说法与拼写

entries.definition: the science of flight and aircraft design
entries.definitionCN: 航空学

entries.definition: a small airport, especially in British usage
entries.definitionCN: 小型机场（英式）

entries.definition: a traveller in a balloon or airship
entries.definitionCN: 气球或飞艇的驾驶者

entries.definition: any vehicle that flies, including helicopters; broader than aeroplane
entries.definitionCN: 任何飞行器，包括直升机；范围比 aeroplane 宽

entries.definition: the short everyday word for an aeroplane
entries.definitionCN: 飞机（口语简称）

entries.definition: an aircraft driven by jet engines
entries.definitionCN: 喷气式飞机

entries.definition: an aircraft that flies without an engine
entries.definitionCN: 滑翔机

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, air and wandering, plus the French ending that names a machine.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊部件「空气」与「游荡」，加上法语里指机器的词尾。

normal.en: aero- means air, and -plane here comes from a Greek word for wandering.
normal.cn: aero- 表示「空气」，这里的 -plane 来自希腊语「游荡」。

normal.en: British travellers say aeroplane; American travellers say airplane.
normal.cn: 英国旅客说 aeroplane，美国旅客说 airplane。

normal.en: A paper aeroplane keeps the shape but loses the engine.
normal.cn: 纸飞机保留了形状，却没有了发动机。

normal.en: The same aero- appears in aerodrome and aeronautics.
normal.cn: 同一个 aero- 也出现在 aerodrome 与 aeronautics 中。

normal.en: Spell it with aero-, not airo-.
normal.cn: 拼写用 aero-，不要写成 airo-。

abstract.en: Picture a white machine wandering through a grey sky like a fish through water.
abstract.cn: 想象一架白色机器像鱼游过水一样，在灰色天空里游走。

abstract.en: See a child's hand release a folded wing that wanders to the far wall.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子的手放开一只折出的翅膀，它一路游荡到远墙。

abstract.en: Imagine the same word shrinking from a machine to a toy and keeping its name.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词从机器缩成玩具，却仍留着原来的名字。

examples.en: The aeroplane from Paris landed ten minutes late.
examples.cn: 从巴黎飞来的飞机晚了十分钟降落。

examples.en: They crossed the mountains by aeroplane instead of by train.
examples.cn: 他们没有坐火车，而是乘飞机越过群山。

examples.en: A paper aeroplane sailed from the back row to the teacher's desk.
examples.cn: 一架纸飞机从后排滑到讲台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱若普兰」——爱若飘在空气里，就折成一架飞机让它慢慢游。

root: 法语 aéroplane 由希腊语 aer「空气」与 planos「游荡的」构成，十九世纪中期造出，指固定翼飞行器；英语借入后成为英式常用词。

sensesIntro.en: One sense names the machine, the other names the shape; both go wandering through the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项指那台机器，另一个义项指那个形状；两者都在空中游走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine wandering through a grey sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架白色机器在灰色天空中游走。

branches.en: a plane climbing above the clouds
branches.cn: 爬升到云上的飞机

branches.en: a late flight from Paris
branches.cn: 从巴黎晚点到达的航班

branches.en: a folded paper wing crossing a classroom
branches.cn: 飞过教室的折纸翅膀

branches.en: a model hanging from a child's ceiling
branches.cn: 挂在孩子房间天花板上的模型

branches.en: the machine and its small imitation
branches.cn: 机器本身与它的小小仿制品

intro.en: A Greek word for air, a Greek word for wandering, and a French ending.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语的「空气」、一个希腊语的「游荡」，再加一个法语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, not Latin, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这些部件来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 航空航天（地球大气层与外层空间的合称）；航空航天工业
definition_en: the earth’s atmosphere together with outer space, considered as one region; the industry that builds aircraft and spacecraft
core_image: 把大气层和外层空间当成同一片地方
scene: 厂房一头装着机翼，另一头装着火箭整流罩。The aerospace plant employs half the town.
sceneCN: 这里 aerospace 是「航空航天工业」（第 2 个义项：制造飞行器与航天器的产业）；句意为这家航空航天工厂雇了镇上一半的人。核心画面是把大气层与外层空间当成同一片地方。

pos.zh: 航空航天；航空航天工业

derivatives.zh: 同族复合词，由 air 加 space 构成，义为「空域」，只指大气层内
同族复合词，由 space 加 craft 构成，义为「航天器」
同族复合词，由 aero- 加 drome「跑道」构成，义为「机场」

senses.title: The atmosphere and outer space as one region
senses.definition: the earth’s atmosphere and the space beyond it, treated together as a single continuous region
senses.definitionCN: 地球大气层与其外的空间，被当作一个连续的整体区域
senses.example: Vehicles crossing aerospace must survive both air and vacuum.
senses.exampleCN: 穿越航空航天的飞行器必须同时承受空气与真空。
senses.why: Aero means air and space means the void beyond it, so the compound deliberately refuses to draw a line where the atmosphere thins away.
senses.whyCN: aero 意为「空气」，space 意为其外的虚空，所以这个复合词刻意不在大气变稀处划线。

senses.title: The industry that builds for both
senses.definition: the sector of industry that designs and manufactures aircraft, missiles and spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 设计制造飞行器、导弹与航天器的工业部门
senses.example: Aerospace is the region’s largest employer.
senses.exampleCN: 航空航天业是该地区最大的雇主。
senses.why: Once the region had one name, the factories serving it took that name too, which is how a word for a place became a word for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这片区域有了统一的名字，为它服务的工厂也就沿用了这个名字——一个地点词由此变成产业词。

intro.en: Aerospace is a modern American compound, coined because rockets made the old border between air and space useless.
intro.cn: aerospace 是现代美式复合词，它的出现是因为火箭让空气与空间之间的旧边界失效了。

items.en: Greek aer, air, supplies the first element through the combining form aero-.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer「空气」通过组合形式 aero- 提供第一个成分。
